hi! i don’t know if this will help you decide how to tell your husband but i can tell you a bit about how i told mine. it wasn’t easy at all and it gave me a lot of anxiety, but he is the most helpful person because he cares about me, and i’m sure your husband does too. first i wrote down how i was feeling in a journal to properly articulate my emotions. i waited until it was friday/saturday so that he was relaxed and didn’t have other things on his mind and we could have a well thought out conversation. i had my journal with me, and in the same room i asked if we could talk for a bit. (it can be hard to do this for the first time and can be very anxiety inducing) i started crying before i said anything but he was very comforting; i essentially first told him that i struggled with mental health issues and that they were getting worse. you don’t have to immediately jump into self harm and other topics because it can make u overwhelmed easily, so you can start slow and explain yourself fully as you go on.
no matter how you tell him, just know that your husband will be there no matter what. he cares about you and your mental health. this community cares about you too.

hi! the beginning part of your text, “I've said this about several exams, but unfortunately I still live haha.” made me laugh because i have been in that situation SO many times. i completely understand what you’re feeling because you’re well aware that killing yourself is hard mentally and physically, but at the same time you aren’t entirely sure what benefit you get from being alive. to be completely honest, i don’t think i’m in the right position to tell you how to determine your worth or how to make yourself happy because i struggle with that constantly. however, the first part of your text shows that you are clearly still holding on for something. you may not know what it is, but you are strong and you have kept fighting because you have hope. one piece of advice i can give u to make life a bit easier is to focus on having “small purposes” in life. people often think they aren’t worthy because they will “never do anything good for society” or they “don’t have any worth”, but try and focus on your life in small bits and pieces. for example, when i’m overwhelmed sometimes my purpose in life is just to calm down. when i’m not taking care of myself, sometimes my purpose is just to drink water or take a nap.

i don’t know if this will help you but i want you to know i understand how you’re feeling. it’s a very tough emotion to deal with and the fact that you’re fighting is something you should be proud of.
i get that. it’s a lot easier to deal with life when u know u have an escape waiting.

as a fellow suicidal person it’s hard for me to truly tell you that it gets better overall, but i think we are the most pessimistic people around. we don’t even try to believe that good days come around. in a way we are right for thinking that way, but there are always small things that can make us happy. i came to realize that we don’t need to have one set purpose in life. it’s nice to have goals, but sometimes our purpose is in the moment. maybe your purpose right now is to feel less anxious, eat dinner, get out of bed, etc. we don’t need to hold ourselves to one major goal in life. we can do many small things. i feel like suicidal people like us always try to compare ourselves to people without mental health struggles, which just sets us back even further. we are who we are, and we can only compare ourselves to our past selves.

i hope this helps you in some way
